safety.student_notice: Don't include personal or identifying information in your answers.
safety.scope_guard: Description level only. The practice never asks for, and the coach never invites, a real document, real employee or customer data, a contract, medical or financial information, or any real identifying detail. If a student pastes something that looks real, the coach tells them to replace it with a description.

personal_path_ui.resource_prefix: Optional extra resource (further reading, not required):

checks: sources trace to the Module 1 architecture rather than being invented
includes at least one non-document source (user input, process data, or model output)
t1_inventory.common_miss: Lists only uploaded documents and forgets the user's typed question and the model's answer (slide 7).

checks: uses the four level names: public, internal, confidential, restricted
gives a reason per source, not just a label
distinguishes the data owner from the process owner
t2_classification.common_miss: Everything is labelled Internal, or the person interviewed in Module 2 is written in as the data owner.

checks: names roles rather than real people
includes InfoSec/CISO or DPO where confidential or personal data is involved
carries a concrete question per stakeholder
t3_stakeholders.common_miss: One generic 'ask IT' with no question, or no escalation point named at all.

checks: at least five of the ten items addressed
separates what is already in place from what is still open
does not claim an item is done without saying who does it
t4_controls.common_miss: All ten marked done, which means the checklist was not really applied.

checks: reports something the partner changed or challenged
names the hidden Confidential item found, or says honestly that none was found
t5_pairs.common_miss: Confirms the partner agreed with everything, which usually means the challenge did not happen.

outcome_logic.when: t2 uses fewer than two distinct levels
outcome_logic.path: Re-open the summary table on slide 16 and re-sort your inventory. If every source really is one level, write the sentence that proves it for the two you are least sure about.

outcome_logic.when: t2 names no data owner, or the data owner equals the process owner everywhere
outcome_logic.path: Separate the two roles for at least one source before the homework. Ask who is formally accountable for the source, then ask who approves its use.

outcome_logic.when: t1 has no user input, process data or model output
outcome_logic.path: Add the model's own answer to the inventory and classify it. It is data, and it is logged.

outcome_logic.when: t3 names no InfoSec/CISO or DPO while confidential or personal data appears in t2
outcome_logic.path: Add the escalation point. Confidential and above needs the data owner plus InfoSec or the DPO, and you must not decide the exposure level alone.

outcome_logic.when: t4 addresses fewer than five items
outcome_logic.path: Fill the remaining items to five before you leave the room, and mark each as in place or still open. The open ones are what you carry into Part A.
You have what Part A needs. Write the one-sentence rationale for every source, then list your three open questions. Those are the entry condition to the build modules.
